heading: About Me
paragraphs: My interest in problem-solving first took shape through mathematics and physics competitions. Placing third in a national junior-level Olympiad in 2016 was an early milestone. What has stayed with me is the satisfaction of working through a difficult problem and finally understanding why the answer makes sense.

Teaching has added another side to that experience. With students preparing for school exams and university admission, getting an answer is only part of the work. Finding an explanation that someone can follow takes patience, careful listening, and a willingness to try a different approach.

I bring that way of thinking to software and research. I enjoy tracing a problem through its details: the steps a person takes through an interface, the assumptions behind an implementation, or the reasoning behind a model's response. The part I find most rewarding is reaching an explanation I can put into practice and share with someone else.
